# Backend

## Overview

The backend is a Java 21 Spring Boot application. Spring gRPC serves frame management on port 9090. Spring MVC and Actuator serve health endpoints on port 8080. Spring Boot applies Flyway migrations against PostgreSQL at startup. The Docker image builds a Spring Boot JAR and runs it on Java 21. [build.gradle:languageVersion] [build.gradle:dependencies] [Dockerfile:RUN] [Dockerfile:ENTRYPOINT]

## Subdirectories & Boundaries

- [Source tree](./src/README.md) contains the application and its runtime configuration.
- [Inventory migration](./src/main/resources/db/migration/V1__create_frame_inventory.sql) creates the frame, version history, and related tables.
- [Frame inventory schema](../../docs/frame-inventory-schema/frame-inventory-schema.md) maps the CSV fields and describes the shared Spring write transaction.

## Local development

Start the Compose PostgreSQL service from the repository root with
`docker compose up -d --wait postgres`. From `src/backend`, run
`./gradlew bootRun` with Java 21. The local JDBC defaults connect to the
Compose database. Set `SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL`, `SPRING_DATASOURCE_USERNAME`,
and `SPRING_DATASOURCE_PASSWORD` when connecting to a different database.

## Verification

From `src/backend`, run `./gradlew test` with Java 21 and Docker available. The
suite covers unit tests and calls the gRPC service through a generated client
against PostgreSQL 18.6 using Testcontainers. Flyway applies both schema
migrations during the integration tests.

## Frame management API

The [Protobuf definition](src/main/proto/frameinventory/v1/frames.proto) declares
the six RPCs. Run `./gradlew generateProto` to generate the Java messages and
stubs. The [API contract](../../docs/frame-management-grpc-api.md#grpc-contract) describes
pagination, request fields, errors, and version checks.

With the backend running, call the service from `src/backend` using `grpcurl`.

```sh
grpcurl -plaintext -import-path src/main/proto -proto frameinventory/v1/frames.proto \
  -d '{"page":0,"size":25}' localhost:9090 frameinventory.v1.FrameManagement/ListFrames
```

The backend writes structured JSON logs to the console. Set
`LOGGING_LEVEL_COM_GLOBAL_CT_FRAMEINVENTORY_FRAME=DEBUG` to include frame RPC
parameters, version checks, lookup results, and handled client errors.

## Sentry error reporting

Set `SENTRY_DSN` to the DSN of the backend's Sentry project and set
`SENTRY_ENVIRONMENT` to the environment name, such as `staging`. The environment
defaults to `local`. An empty or unset DSN disables error reporting.

Export the variables before running `./gradlew bootRun` from `src/backend`.
For Docker Compose, export the same variables or set them in an untracked
`.env` file at the repository root, then run `docker compose up --build -d backend`
to rebuild and apply the settings.

To verify reporting, use a non-production Sentry project or environment. In a
local checkout, temporarily make a controller handler throw an
`IllegalStateException` with a unique test message and call that route. Confirm
the event appears in Sentry with the expected stack trace and environment tag,
then link the event on the issue. Remove the temporary exception and confirm
`curl --fail http://localhost:8080/api/health` succeeds with the DSN configured
and again after restarting the backend with the DSN unset.

### Local import operator

The import RPC service attaches `LocalImportIdentity` as a service-scoped
interceptor. Existing frame RPCs do not use it. Enable Spring's `local-import`
profile only for host-local development and set `INVENTORY_IMPORT_LOCAL_TOKEN`
to a randomly generated 64-character lowercase hex value. Keep the credential
out of source control and logs. The RPC accepts the credential as
`authorization: Bearer <token>` only from a loopback peer and sets the fixed
`local-import-operator` identity. The interceptor checks the actual transport
peer. The Spring gRPC server can still listen on all interfaces.

The import BFF must run on the same host, accept the credential only for import
operations, and forward it alongside the existing correlation metadata. Do not
derive operator identity from a browser-supplied ID or treat ordinary frame RPC
authentication as an import credential. The single local operator can create
DELTA jobs and request force overwrite. The service rejects FULL_SNAPSHOT until the snapshot safety checks ship. Persist the verified
operator as job owner and check ownership before returning status or row
diagnostics. Production imports remain disabled until an operator identity
provider and permission policy are configured.


### Local import RPCs

Start PostgreSQL and the `aws` Compose service. Run Spring Boot on the host
with the `local-import` profile and configure these additional variables:

| Variable | Local value |
| --- | --- |
| `INVENTORY_IMPORT_BUCKET` | `frame-inventory-import-local` |
| `INVENTORY_IMPORT_REGION` | `us-east-1` |
| `INVENTORY_IMPORT_SIGNING_ENDPOINT` | `http://127.0.0.1:4566` |
| `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` | `test` |
| `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` | `test` |

`InventoryImport.CreateImportJob` creates a DELTA job and returns a PUT URL
valid for 15 minutes. Send every returned header unchanged, including
`If-None-Match: *` and the CSV content type. The caller can read the durable
summary with `GetImportJob` and the diagnostics with `ListImportRowErrors`.
Diagnostics are ordered by data row number and error code. Pages are zero-based
and default to 25 items.

`AWAITING_UPLOAD` becomes `PENDING` when dispatch binds the first accepted
object version. Dispatch must validate the event and pass the upload time and
the decoded key to the repository. A timely upload may arrive for another
# Frame Inventory BFF

From the repository root, run `docker compose up --build bff`. Open [Apollo Sandbox](http://127.0.0.1:4000) and run:

```graphql
query ListFrames {
  frames(page: 0, size: 25) {
    items {
      frameId
      versionId
      attributes {
        status
        address
      }
    }
    page
    size
    hasNext
  }
}
```

The query uses the backend's zero-based pagination. Omitted arguments use page
`0` and size `25`. Sizes from `1` through `50` are valid. An empty inventory
returns an empty list with `hasNext: false`.

When Spring rejects invalid input, the GraphQL error has code `BAD_USER_INPUT`.
If the backend supplies validation details, `extensions.fieldViolations`
contains `{ field, description }` entries using backend property paths.
Other input errors may not include this extension.

## Frame lifecycle in Apollo Sandbox

Paste these operations into Sandbox. Run **Create** with variables
`{"id":"sandbox-frame-001"}`. Use a fresh ID for each run, since Spring reserves
frame IDs after their first use, including after deletion.

```graphql
fragment Snapshot on Frame {
  frameId
  versionId
  current
  validFrom
  validTo
  changeSource
  closedByChangeSource
  attributes {
    status
    address
  }
}

mutation Create($id: ID!) {
  createFrame(
    frameId: $id
    attributes: { status: DRAFT, address: "Test site" }
  ) {
    ...Snapshot
  }
}

query Read($id: ID!) {
  frame(frameId: $id) {
    ...Snapshot
  }
}

mutation Update($id: ID!, $version: String!) {
  updateFrame(
    frameId: $id
    expectedVersionId: $version
    attributes: { status: LIVE, address: "Test site" }
  ) {
    ...Snapshot
  }
}

query History($id: ID!) {
  frameHistory(frameId: $id) {
    ...Snapshot
  }
}

mutation Delete($id: ID!, $version: String!) {
  deleteFrame(frameId: $id, expectedVersionId: $version)
}
```

1. Run **Read** to confirm the frame exists. Copy the returned `versionId` into
   the `version` variable as a JSON string and run **Update**. Updates replace
   writable attributes, so include any optional values you want to retain.
2. Run **History** to see the new version followed by the original. Running
   **Update** again with the original version should return `CONFLICT`.
3. Set `version` to the version returned by **Update**, then run **Delete**.
   Expect `true`. **Read** returns `NOT_FOUND` and **History** still shows both
   versions, with `MANUAL_DELETE` closing the latest one.

## Local development

To run the BFF outside Docker, start the backend, then run `npm ci`,
`npm run build`, and `npm start` from `src/bff`. The build generates TypeScript
types from the backend's Protobuf definition and copies `frames.proto` into
`dist/proto/` for the gRPC client. Set `FRAME_GRPC_ENDPOINT` to the Spring gRPC
endpoint as `host:port`. It defaults to `localhost:9090` for local runs and
`backend:9090` in Docker Compose.

Apollo loads the `.gql` schema files from [`schema/`](./schema/) at startup.
The resolver implementations live in [`src/resolvers/`](./src/resolvers/).
The build runs GraphQL Codegen to generate TypeScript resolver types from the
same files. Run `npm run codegen` to regenerate the resolver types on their own.

For a local run, Apollo's OpenTelemetry metrics are available at
`http://127.0.0.1:9465/metrics`. They cover requests that enter Apollo's GraphQL
pipeline. Parse, validation, and resolver errors count as failed requests.
Request metrics use operation type and outcome. A separate histogram measures
top-level resolver time, including upstream gRPC calls, by operation type and
schema field name. Client-chosen operation names and aliases are excluded from
the labels. See the [BFF metrics dashboard](../../README.md#bff-metrics) for the
Compose setup.

Run `npm run lint` and `npm run format:check` to check the BFF. Run
`npm run format` to apply Prettier. Run `npm test` to generate types, type-check
the test, and run it through ts-jest with a stub gRPC client.

## Sentry error reporting

Set `SENTRY_DSN` to the BFF Sentry project's DSN before starting the service.
For Compose, set `BFF_SENTRY_DSN` instead. Set `SENTRY_ENVIRONMENT` to label events by
deployment environment. An unset or empty DSN leaves reporting disabled.

Apollo reports unexpected execution errors, internal server errors, and
upstream unavailability. Expected GraphQL validation and domain errors are
excluded. The SDK strips request data and breadcrumbs from reported events.

## Local inventory import

The BFF build packages both the frame and inventory import protobufs. For local
imports, run Spring Boot and the BFF on the same host. Enable Spring's
`local-import` profile and configure its S3 upload settings as described in the
[backend README](../backend/README.md). Set
`IMPORT_GRPC_ENDPOINT=127.0.0.1:9090` on the BFF. This makes the BFF listen on
IPv4 loopback and limits the import gRPC target to IPv4 loopback. With the
variable unset, the import resolvers return `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` and frame
operations remain available.

Send the local operator token as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` with
`createImportJob`, `importJob`, and `importRowErrors`. Only these resolvers
forward the credential to Spring, which verifies the token and checks job
ownership. Use the returned `uploadHeaders` values for the direct S3 PUT, then
poll the job and request row errors by page. Keep the credential and signed
URL out of application logs.
FROM eclipse-temurin:21-jdk AS build
WORKDIR /workspace
COPY gradle gradle
COPY gradlew settings.gradle build.gradle ./
COPY src src
RUN ./gradlew --no-daemon bootJar

FROM eclipse-temurin:21-jdk
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=build /workspace/build/libs/*.jar app.jar
EXPOSE 8080 9090
ENTRYPOINT ["java", "-jar", "/app/app.jar"]
FROM node:22-alpine AS build
WORKDIR /app/bff
COPY bff/package.json bff/package-lock.json ./
RUN npm ci
COPY backend/src/main/proto/ /app/backend/src/main/proto/
COPY bff/codegen.yml bff/tsconfig.json ./
COPY bff/schema/ ./schema/
COPY bff/src/ ./src/
RUN npm run build && npm prune --omit=dev

FROM node:22-alpine AS runtime
WORKDIR /app/bff
COPY --from=build /app/bff/node_modules ./node_modules
COPY --from=build /app/bff/dist ./dist
COPY --from=build /app/bff/schema ./schema
USER node
EXPOSE 4000 9465
CMD ["node", "dist/index.js"]
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

ready_file=/tmp/inventory-import-ready
rm -f "$ready_file"
bucket=frame-inventory-import-local

awslocal s3api create-bucket --bucket "$bucket"
awslocal s3api put-bucket-versioning --bucket "$bucket" \
  --versioning-configuration Status=Enabled
awslocal s3api put-bucket-cors --bucket "$bucket" \
  --cors-configuration '{"CORSRules":[{"AllowedOrigins":["http://localhost:3000","http://127.0.0.1:3000"],"AllowedMethods":["PUT"],"AllowedHeaders":["Content-Type","If-None-Match"],"ExposeHeaders":["ETag","x-amz-version-id"]}]}'

dlq_url=$(awslocal sqs create-queue --queue-name inventory-import-dlq \
  --query QueueUrl --output text)
dlq_arn=$(awslocal sqs get-queue-attributes --queue-url "$dlq_url" \
  --attribute-names QueueArn --query Attributes.QueueArn --output text)
queue_url=$(awslocal sqs create-queue --queue-name inventory-import \
  --query QueueUrl --output text)
queue_arn=$(awslocal sqs get-queue-attributes --queue-url "$queue_url" \
  --attribute-names QueueArn --query Attributes.QueueArn --output text)

attributes=$(python3 - "$queue_arn" "$dlq_arn" "$bucket" <<'PY'
import json
import sys

queue, dlq, bucket = sys.argv[1:]
print(json.dumps({
    "VisibilityTimeout": "120",
    "ReceiveMessageWaitTimeSeconds": "20",
    "RedrivePolicy": json.dumps({"deadLetterTargetArn": dlq, "maxReceiveCount": 5}),
    "Policy": json.dumps({"Version": "2012-10-17", "Statement": [{
        "Effect": "Allow",
        "Principal": {"Service": "s3.amazonaws.com"},
        "Action": "sqs:SendMessage",
        "Resource": queue,
        "Condition": {"ArnEquals": {"aws:SourceArn": f"arn:aws:s3:::{bucket}"}},
    }]}),
}))
PY
)
awslocal sqs set-queue-attributes --queue-url "$queue_url" --attributes "$attributes"
awslocal s3api put-bucket-notification-configuration --bucket "$bucket" \
  --notification-configuration "{
    \"QueueConfigurations\": [{
      \"QueueArn\": \"$queue_arn\",
      \"Events\": [\"s3:ObjectCreated:Put\"],
      \"Filter\": {\"Key\": {\"FilterRules\": [
        {\"Name\": \"prefix\", \"Value\": \"uploads/\"},
        {\"Name\": \"suffix\", \"Value\": \"/inventory_frame.csv\"}
      ]}}
    }]
  }"
touch "$ready_file"

then link the event on the issue. Remove the temporary exception and confirm
`curl --fail http://localhost:8080/api/health` succeeds with the DSN configured
and again after restarting the backend with the DSN unset.

### Local import operator

The import RPC service attaches `LocalImportIdentity` as a service-scoped
interceptor. Existing frame RPCs do not use it. Enable Spring's `local-import`
profile only for host-local development and set `INVENTORY_IMPORT_LOCAL_TOKEN`
to a randomly generated 64-character lowercase hex value. Keep the credential
out of source control and logs. The RPC accepts the credential as
`authorization: Bearer <token>` only from a loopback peer and sets the fixed
`local-import-operator` identity. The interceptor checks the actual transport
peer. The Spring gRPC server can still listen on all interfaces.

The import BFF must run on the same host, accept the credential only for import
operations, and forward it alongside the existing correlation metadata. Do not
derive operator identity from a browser-supplied ID or treat ordinary frame RPC
authentication as an import credential. The single local operator can create
DELTA jobs and request force overwrite. The service rejects FULL_SNAPSHOT until the snapshot safety checks ship. Persist the verified
operator as job owner and check ownership before returning status or row
diagnostics. Production imports remain disabled until an operator identity
provider and permission policy are configured.


### Local import RPCs

Start PostgreSQL and the `aws` Compose service. Run Spring Boot on the host
with the `local-import` profile and configure these additional variables:

| Variable | Local value |
| --- | --- |
| `INVENTORY_IMPORT_BUCKET` | `frame-inventory-import-local` |
| `INVENTORY_IMPORT_REGION` | `us-east-1` |
| `INVENTORY_IMPORT_SIGNING_ENDPOINT` | `http://127.0.0.1:4566` |
| `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` | `test` |
| `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` | `test` |

`InventoryImport.CreateImportJob` creates a DELTA job and returns a PUT URL
valid for 15 minutes. Send every returned header unchanged, including
`If-None-Match: *` and the CSV content type. The caller can read the durable
summary with `GetImportJob` and the diagnostics with `ListImportRowErrors`.
Diagnostics are ordered by data row number and error code. Pages are zero-based
and default to 25 items.

`AWAITING_UPLOAD` becomes `PENDING` when dispatch binds the first accepted
object version. Dispatch must validate the event and pass the upload time and
the decoded key to the repository. A timely upload may arrive for another
# Frame Inventory BFF

From the repository root, run `docker compose up --build bff`. Open [Apollo Sandbox](http://127.0.0.1:4000) and run:

```graphql
query ListFrames {
  frames(page: 0, size: 25) {
    items {
      frameId
      versionId
      attributes {
        status
        address
      }
    }
    page
    size
    hasNext
  }
}
```

The query uses the backend's zero-based pagination. Omitted arguments use page
`0` and size `25`. Sizes from `1` through `50` are valid. An empty inventory
returns an empty list with `hasNext: false`.

When Spring rejects invalid input, the GraphQL error has code `BAD_USER_INPUT`.
If the backend supplies validation details, `extensions.fieldViolations`
contains `{ field, description }` entries using backend property paths.
Other input errors may not include this extension.

## Frame lifecycle in Apollo Sandbox

Paste these operations into Sandbox. Run **Create** with variables
`{"id":"sandbox-frame-001"}`. Use a fresh ID for each run, since Spring reserves
frame IDs after their first use, including after deletion.

```graphql
fragment Snapshot on Frame {
  frameId
  versionId
  current
  validFrom
  validTo
  changeSource
  closedByChangeSource
  attributes {
    status
    address
  }
}

mutation Create($id: ID!) {
  createFrame(
    frameId: $id
    attributes: { status: DRAFT, address: "Test site" }
  ) {
    ...Snapshot
  }
}

query Read($id: ID!) {
  frame(frameId: $id) {
    ...Snapshot
  }
}

mutation Update($id: ID!, $version: String!) {
  updateFrame(
    frameId: $id
    expectedVersionId: $version
    attributes: { status: LIVE, address: "Test site" }
  ) {
    ...Snapshot
  }
}

query History($id: ID!) {
  frameHistory(frameId: $id) {
    ...Snapshot
  }
}

mutation Delete($id: ID!, $version: String!) {
  deleteFrame(frameId: $id, expectedVersionId: $version)
}
```

1. Run **Read** to confirm the frame exists. Copy the returned `versionId` into
   the `version` variable as a JSON string and run **Update**. Updates replace
   writable attributes, so include any optional values you want to retain.
2. Run **History** to see the new version followed by the original. Running
   **Update** again with the original version should return `CONFLICT`.
3. Set `version` to the version returned by **Update**, then run **Delete**.
   Expect `true`. **Read** returns `NOT_FOUND` and **History** still shows both
   versions, with `MANUAL_DELETE` closing the latest one.

## Local development

To run the BFF outside Docker, start the backend, then run `npm ci`,
`npm run build`, and `npm start` from `src/bff`. The build generates TypeScript
types from the backend's Protobuf definition and copies `frames.proto` into
`dist/proto/` for the gRPC client. Set `FRAME_GRPC_ENDPOINT` to the Spring gRPC
endpoint as `host:port`. It defaults to `localhost:9090` for local runs and
`backend:9090` in Docker Compose.

Apollo loads the `.gql` schema files from [`schema/`](./schema/) at startup.
The resolver implementations live in [`src/resolvers/`](./src/resolvers/).
The build runs GraphQL Codegen to generate TypeScript resolver types from the
same files. Run `npm run codegen` to regenerate the resolver types on their own.

For a local run, Apollo's OpenTelemetry metrics are available at
`http://127.0.0.1:9465/metrics`. They cover requests that enter Apollo's GraphQL
pipeline. Parse, validation, and resolver errors count as failed requests.
Request metrics use operation type and outcome. A separate histogram measures
top-level resolver time, including upstream gRPC calls, by operation type and
schema field name. Client-chosen operation names and aliases are excluded from
the labels. See the [BFF metrics dashboard](../../README.md#bff-metrics) for the
Compose setup.

Run `npm run lint` and `npm run format:check` to check the BFF. Run
`npm run format` to apply Prettier. Run `npm test` to generate types, type-check
the test, and run it through ts-jest with a stub gRPC client.

## Sentry error reporting

Set `SENTRY_DSN` to the BFF Sentry project's DSN before starting the service.
For Compose, set `BFF_SENTRY_DSN` instead. Set `SENTRY_ENVIRONMENT` to label events by
deployment environment. An unset or empty DSN leaves reporting disabled.

Apollo reports unexpected execution errors, internal server errors, and
upstream unavailability. Expected GraphQL validation and domain errors are
excluded. The SDK strips request data and breadcrumbs from reported events.

## Local inventory import

The BFF build packages both the frame and inventory import protobufs. For local
imports, run Spring Boot and the BFF on the same host. Enable Spring's
`local-import` profile and configure its S3 upload settings as described in the
[backend README](../backend/README.md). Set
`IMPORT_GRPC_ENDPOINT=127.0.0.1:9090` on the BFF. This makes the BFF listen on
IPv4 loopback and limits the import gRPC target to IPv4 loopback. With the
variable unset, the import resolvers return `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` and frame
operations remain available.

Send the local operator token as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` with
`createImportJob`, `importJob`, and `importRowErrors`. Only these resolvers
forward the credential to Spring, which verifies the token and checks job
ownership. Use the returned `uploadHeaders` values for the direct S3 PUT, then
poll the job and request row errors by page. Keep the credential and signed
URL out of application logs.
FROM eclipse-temurin:21-jdk AS build
WORKDIR /workspace
COPY gradle gradle
COPY gradlew settings.gradle build.gradle ./
COPY src src
RUN ./gradlew --no-daemon bootJar

FROM eclipse-temurin:21-jdk
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=build /workspace/build/libs/*.jar app.jar
EXPOSE 8080 9090
ENTRYPOINT ["java", "-jar", "/app/app.jar"]
FROM node:22-alpine AS build
WORKDIR /app/bff
COPY bff/package.json bff/package-lock.json ./
RUN npm ci
COPY backend/src/main/proto/ /app/backend/src/main/proto/
COPY bff/codegen.yml bff/tsconfig.json ./
COPY bff/schema/ ./schema/
COPY bff/src/ ./src/
RUN npm run build && npm prune --omit=dev

FROM node:22-alpine AS runtime
WORKDIR /app/bff
COPY --from=build /app/bff/node_modules ./node_modules
COPY --from=build /app/bff/dist ./dist
COPY --from=build /app/bff/schema ./schema
USER node
EXPOSE 4000 9465
CMD ["node", "dist/index.js"]

ready_file=/tmp/inventory-import-ready

bucket=frame-inventory-import-local

awslocal s3api create-bucket --bucket "$bucket"
awslocal s3api put-bucket-versioning --bucket "$bucket" \
  --versioning-configuration Status=Enabled
awslocal s3api put-bucket-cors --bucket "$bucket" \
  --cors-configuration '{"CORSRules":[{"AllowedOrigins":["http://localhost:3000","http://127.0.0.1:3000"],"AllowedMethods":["PUT"],"AllowedHeaders":["Content-Type","If-None-Match"],"ExposeHeaders":["ETag","x-amz-version-id"]}]}'

dlq_url=$(awslocal sqs create-queue --queue-name inventory-import-dlq \
  --query QueueUrl --output text)
dlq_arn=$(awslocal sqs get-queue-attributes --queue-url "$dlq_url" \
  --attribute-names QueueArn --query Attributes.QueueArn --output text)
queue_url=$(awslocal sqs create-queue --queue-name inventory-import \
  --query QueueUrl --output text)
queue_arn=$(awslocal sqs get-queue-attributes --queue-url "$queue_url" \
  --attribute-names QueueArn --query Attributes.QueueArn --output text)

attributes=$(python3 - "$queue_arn" "$dlq_arn" "$bucket" <<'PY'
import json
import sys

queue, dlq, bucket = sys.argv[1:]
print(json.dumps({
    "VisibilityTimeout": "120",
    "ReceiveMessageWaitTimeSeconds": "20",
    "RedrivePolicy": json.dumps({"deadLetterTargetArn": dlq, "maxReceiveCount": 5}),
    "Policy": json.dumps({"Version": "2012-10-17", "Statement": [{
        "Effect": "Allow",
        "Principal": {"Service": "s3.amazonaws.com"},
        "Action": "sqs:SendMessage",
        "Resource": queue,
        "Condition": {"ArnEquals": {"aws:SourceArn": f"arn:aws:s3:::{bucket}"}},
    }]}),
}))
PY
)
awslocal sqs set-queue-attributes --queue-url "$queue_url" --attributes "$attributes"
awslocal s3api put-bucket-notification-configuration --bucket "$bucket" \
  --notification-configuration "{
    \"QueueConfigurations\": [{
      \"QueueArn\": \"$queue_arn\",
      \"Events\": [\"s3:ObjectCreated:Put\"],
      \"Filter\": {\"Key\": {\"FilterRules\": [
        {\"Name\": \"prefix\", \"Value\": \"uploads/\"},
        {\"Name\": \"suffix\", \"Value\": \"/inventory_frame.csv\"}
      ]}}
    }]
  }"
touch "$ready_file"

5. Verify behavior through the normal entry points.

   - Create backend tests under `src/backend/src/test/java/com/global/ct/frameinventory/inventoryimport/`. Use `InventoryCsvReaderTests.java` for the supplied CSV, multiline fields, empty files, missing IDs, duplicate IDs, exact byte and logical-row limits, hash stability, and UTC timestamp parsing under non-UTC JVM and database session settings. Use `ImportDispatchTests.java` for native envelopes, test events, duplicates, delayed delivery, and ambiguous starts followed by DLQ. Use `ImportApplyTests.java` with PostgreSQL 18 for the full apply transaction, idempotent retries, legacy and manual edits, force restoration, reactivation, and rollback without inventory or watermark changes. |---|---|

# Inventory import infrastructure

This Terraform root provisions a dedicated versioned S3 bucket, a standard SQS
queue, and a dead-letter queue in one region. S3 sends PUT notifications for
`uploads/*/inventory_frame.csv` directly to the source queue. Attach the
output application policy to the backend's existing execution role. The
backend will use the bucket name and both queue URLs as import configuration.

## Local development

From the repository root:

```sh
docker compose --profile import up -d --wait aws temporal
```

The profile pins the LocalStack community image from before token activation
became mandatory. It exposes S3/SQS on `127.0.0.1:4566` and Temporal on
`127.0.0.1:7233` with UI on port 8233. Containers on the Compose network can
reach `aws:4566` and `temporal:7233`. Use the loopback S3 endpoint
with path-style addressing when signing URLs for a host browser. The ready hook
creates the bucket, queues and notification. The smoke test is intended to run
before starting a queue consumer.

```sh
AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=REDACTED AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=REDACTED uv run infra/inventory-import/smoke.py \
  --endpoint http://127.0.0.1:4566 --region us-east-1 \
  --bucket frame-inventory-import-local --origin http://localhost:3000 \
  --queue-url http://127.0.0.1:4566/000000000000/inventory-import \
  --dlq-url http://127.0.0.1:4566/000000000000/inventory-import-dlq
```

## AWS sandbox

Use a dedicated sandbox account or a dedicated stack with idle queues. Configure
a remote state backend before sharing a deployment. An existing S3 state bucket
with locking enabled (`use_lockfile = true`) and a separate key for each
environment is suitable. Store state outside the import bucket. Supply
`aws_region`, `bucket_name`, `name_prefix` and `frontend_origins` with a local
`.tfvars` file or `TF_VAR_*` environment variables.

From this directory, initialize state and review a plan with sandbox
credentials:

```sh
terraform init \
  -backend-config="bucket=$STATE_BUCKET" \
  -backend-config="key=inventory-import/sandbox.tfstate" \
  -backend-config="region=$STATE_REGION" \
  -backend-config="use_lockfile=true"
terraform validate
terraform plan -out=sandbox.tfplan
```

Apply the reviewed plan in the sandbox. AWS recommends allowing up to 15
minutes for first-time S3 versioning to propagate before writing objects.
For static validation without AWS credentials, use
`terraform init -backend=false` followed by `terraform validate`.

Run the same smoke script with sandbox credentials for the application role,
the configured region and frontend origin, and the Terraform bucket and queue
outputs. Omit `--endpoint`. It checks browser CORS headers, a signed create-only
PUT and rejected replay, version-pinned reads, version-bearing notifications,
and DLQ redrive. The script creates one unique test object and deletes only the
matched event from the DLQ. Leave the test object to the lifecycle policy.

S3 makes live upload objects eligible for expiration after seven days. On a
versioned bucket this creates a delete marker. The underlying noncurrent
version is eligible for permanent expiration after one additional day. Cleanup
is asynchronous. Keep workflow and dispatch retries within the seven-day
window. The standard queue retains messages for four days and the DLQ retains
them for up to fourteen days from the original enqueue time.
variable "aws_region" {
  description = "AWS Region for the upload bucket and both queues."
  type        = string
}

variable "bucket_name" {
  description = "Globally unique name for the dedicated upload bucket."
  type        = string
}

variable "name_prefix" {
  description = "Environment-specific prefix for queues and the application policy."
  type        = string

  validation {
    condition     = can(regex("^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,59}$", var.name_prefix))
    error_message = "Use 1–59 ASCII letters, digits, hyphens, or underscores."
  }
}

variable "frontend_origins" {
  description = "Exact browser origins allowed to issue upload PUTs."
  type        = set(string)

  validation {
    condition = length(var.frontend_origins) > 0 && alltrue([
      for origin in var.frontend_origins : can(regex("^https?://[^/*?#[:space:]]+$", origin))
    ])
    error_message = "Provide at least one exact HTTP(S) origin without a path or wildcard."
  }
}

  value = aws_sqs_queue.dead_letters.url

  value = aws_iam_policy.application.arn
}

Which identity provider and deployment environment should GLO-28 target? The repo currently has a loopback-only operator token, and I found no deployed sign-in configuration in the repo or Linear. [GLO-28](https://linear.app/upfrontbeats/issue/GLO-28/define-and-implement-import-authorization)

I’d use the deployment’s existing OIDC provider if it has one. Spring would verify the operator token, DELTA permissions would be required to start a job, and only the job owner could read its summary and diagnostics. Force overwrite would require a separate permission, and `FULL_SNAPSHOT` would stay disabled.
